atoms.b: How Acid Rain Can Harm Food Webs

A_food_web_explains_the_feeding_relationships_between_different_plants_and_animals_in_an_ecosystem._Acid_rain_is_rain_that_has_been_made_acidic_through_exposure_to_dirty_air._((Acidic rain can cause great damage to food webs in ecosystems such as lakes and rivers.))

One_part_of_the_food_web_that_is_especially_affected_by_acid_rain_is_phytoplankton._If_a_large_amount_of_phytoplankton_die,_consumers_such_as_dragonflies_and_fish_will_lose_an_important_food_source...

atoms.a: What could the author’s main reason be for writing this text?
b: ++To show how acid rain can harm food webs in ecosystems.
To try to show the complexity of food webs in different ecosystems.
To simply talk about the nature of acidic rain.

atoms.a: What is some specific evidence for the author’s main reason?
b: ++Phytoplankton are negatively affected by acid rain.
Every animal is affected by acidic rain, no matter the ecosystem.
Animals at the top of the food chain usually eat other animals.

hint.text: Phytoplankton are plant life that live and drift in water. They are often a food source for larger animals.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: Human activities are the main cause of acid rain. Especially since the 1980s, humans have released so many chemicals into the air that they have changed the mix of gases in the atmosphere. Power plants release the majority of harmful gases when they burn fossil fuels, such as coal, to produce electricity. In addition, the exhausts from cars, trucks and buses releases nitrogen oxides and sulphur dioxide into the air. All of these human-made pollutants cause acid rain.

b: ++Humans are mainly responsible for acid rain.
Humans are barely responsible for acid rain.
Power plants and forms of transportation are bad for the environment.

atoms.a: What may the author’s reason be for their claim?
b: ++To display the impact humans can have on the environment.
To look at the development of chemicals released into the air since the 1980s.

atoms.a: Which evidence does the author mention to support their reason?
b: ++ Since the 1980s, humans have released a lot of chemicals into the air.
Power plants release just as much gas as cars.
There is little evidence that humans have done so much harm to the environment.
